profile.headline: Storage and Cloud Infrastructure at NVIDIA
profile.summary: I'm a software developer focusing on large-scale data processing, storage systems, and cloud computing infrastructure. I am passionate about parallel and distributed systems, and have a strong background in systems development, concurrency, and performance.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: During my time at Amazon, I contributed to the development of Amazon Aurora, AWS's cloud-optimized, MySQL-compatible database engine. Early in my time at AWS, my team helped ship the SQL Server engine for the Relational Database Service (RDS).

positions.title: Co-Founder
positions.description: After completing my PhD, I joined my advisor to found a startup company attempting to commercialize novel multi-core programming tools based on techniques developed in my dissertation research.  As a co-founder, I prepared and participated in funding pitches and wrote the technical portion of an application for a Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) grant that was well-reviewed by the National Science Foundation.  I also wrote patent applications and coordinated IP protection with the University's licensing foundation and attorneys.

positions.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
positions.description: While working on a technology transfer startup, I continued to study how to apply determinate parallel programming techniques to large, single-threaded codebases to better understand the challenges involved with parallelizing legacy code and to identify opportunities for better tool support.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: As a graduate student, I performed research in the areas of parallel programming, computer architecture, binary translation, and programming languages. My dissertation research focused on addressing the notorious difficulty of parallel programming by introducing a new parallel programming model that provides the predictability, repeatability, and reliability of the deterministic sequential model. I demonstrated the viability of this programming model by developing a runtime system called Prometheus that uses state-of-the-art dynamic, non-blocking scheduling techniques to achieve performance competitive with conventional multi-threaded programs.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Prepared and delivered lectures for introductory programming course in Java, earning a 4.5/5.0
evaluation average; contributed to assignment and exam development. Graded programming
assignments and homework and provided face-to-face and email support for classes on operating
systems, graphics, and introductory programming.

positions.title: Senior Product Engineer
positions.description: Responsible for yield improvement of ash memory fabrication from process introduction through full-scale production. Identified yield limitations in design, processing, and test and drove to resolution to achieve world-class yields. Supported process transfer from development site to high-volume fabs.

positions.title: Product Engineer
positions.description: Yield analysis and enhancement for CMOS logic and embedded flash technologies.  Responsible for new product introduction from tape-out to wafer-level testing.  Characterized and debugged testing to optimize quality and yield and minimize test time.

positions.title: Applications Engineer Intern
positions.description: As an Applications Engineer intern at NI, I helped streamline Customer Education department operations by developing LotusNotes and LabVIEW applications.
